Hearty Pork Pies for Old Twelfth Night Wassail

Served at: Old Twelfth Night Wassail

Makes 6 individual piesPrep 45 minCook 1 hour 15 min

These savory, hand-held pork pies are a quintessential British comfort food, perfect for serving at a festive Old Twelfth Night Wassail. Traditionally enjoyed cold or at room temperature, they offer a substantial and satisfying bite, ideal for fueling revelers as they bless the apple trees and ward off winter's chill.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (250g) all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (115g) lard, diced
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) water
  • 1 lb (450g) pork shoulder or pork belly, cut into 1/2-inch (1.25cm) cubes
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground mace (optional, but traditional)
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried sage
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) cold water or chicken stock
  • 1 teaspoon unflavored gelatin powder
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and 1 teaspoon of salt. In a small saucepan, combine the lard and 1/2 cup water. Heat gently until the lard has melted and the mixture is hot but not boiling.
  2. Pour the hot lard mixture into the flour, mixing quickly with a wooden spoon until a rough dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently for a few minutes until smooth. Be careful, as it will be warm. Divide the dough into 6 larger pieces (for the bases) and 6 smaller pieces (for the lids). Keep warm under a bowl while you prepare the filling.
  3. In a medium bowl, combine the cubed pork with 1/2 teaspoon salt, pepper, nutmeg, mace (if using), and dried sage. Mix well to ensure the pork is evenly coated.
  4. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 6-cup muffin tin or individual pie molds. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one larger piece of dough into a circle about 5-6 inches (13-15 cm) in diameter. Carefully press it into a muffin tin cup, allowing the edges to come up the sides. Repeat for all 6 bases.
  5. Divide the pork filling evenly among the pastry-lined cups, pressing it down lightly.
  6. Roll out the smaller pieces of dough for the lids. Place a lid over each filled pie. Trim any excess pastry and crimp the edges of the base and lid together to seal. Make a small hole in the center of each pie lid to allow steam to escape.
  7. Brush the tops of the pies with the beaten egg wash.
  8. Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (160°C) and bake for another 55-65 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and the filling is cooked through. If the tops brown too quickly, you can loosely tent them with foil.
  9. While the pies are baking, dissolve the gelatin powder in the cold water or stock. Once the pies are out of the oven, let them cool in the tin for about 15-20 minutes.
  10. Carefully pour a small amount of the gelatin mixture into the hole in the top of each pie. The liquid will seep down and fill any gaps around the meat.
  11. Let the pies cool completely, preferably overnight in the refrigerator, before serving. This allows the jelly to set and the flavors to meld.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, you can add a tablespoon of finely chopped onion or a pinch of dried thyme to the pork filling.
  • Pork pies are traditionally served cold or at room temperature, making them excellent for picnics or buffet-style gatherings.
  • Serve with a dollop of good quality chutney or a sharp mustard for a delightful contrast.
